_comment: Written by the Security Review persona. The pre-tag CI job reads this to decide whether a release is covered by a current audit. Do not hand-edit.
open_findings: HIGH #151: check_deprecated_endpoints no longer covers the shipped bundle. The audit-allow marker added in #149 removes a marked call from both `found` and `hit_dates`, so it contributes neither a finding nor urgency. Probed by mutation from the 8aa9f7a tree: with scripts/rotate-inbound-webhook.py migrated to v2 (that script is inside #101's declared scope), the suite reports 'PASS - no known-deprecated endpoint usage found' at exit 0 while a live GET /v1/webhooks call is still in zaf-build/assets/background.html and still in the bundle members install. The 2026-10-03 escalation to FAIL never fires, because it is driven by an empty hit_dates. The pressure mechanism this record describes is now carried entirely by a file that ships nothing to members, and it disappears when that file is migrated. The marker itself resisted four separate attempts to defeat it; the defect is that its one legitimate use removes the entire shipped artifact from the check's field of view, with no expiry and no re-review trigger. FIX: require `audit-allow: <key> until <YYYY-MM-DD>`, treat an expired marker as FAIL, and make a marker whose entry is inside SUNSET_FAIL_WITHIN_DAYS report at the severity the unmarked call would have.

MEDIUM (on #144, not filed separately): no release exists for either fix. v1.0.54 is the newest tag and the newest GitHub Release; manifest at 8aa9f7a reads 1.0.56. Verified: `git show v1.0.54:zaf-build/assets/background.html` line 73 is `}).catch(function() { _pushRegistered = false; })`, the fail-open probe, and the released bundle still carries all three /collaboration-requests? call sites. The duplicate-inbound-ticket condition #148 exists to remove is live in every install today, and a duplicate is the error direction that reaches the partner. #144 was closed on the merge on 2026-07-29 and REOPENED the same day for this reason; a release acceptance criterion has been added to it.

MEDIUM #153: the residual v1 probe call was tracked by nothing. #144's close comment routed zaf-build/assets/background.html:91 to #101. #101's ZAF-app workstream covers migrating the inbound poll and sync calls to /v2/collaboration-requests, which shipped in #148; its Subscriptions workstream covers migrating each member's own subscription off POST /v1/webhooks. Neither covers deleting this app's GET /v1/webhooks read call. #150 is scoped to the collaboration-request list calls, and Connect-ReleaseMGT#210's connector table lists only the Quick Start registration and rotate-inbound-webhook.py for this repo. This repeats verbatim an error THIS RECORD corrected two commits earlier, in a note stating that #101's scope does not include the ZAF app's own calls; the same wrong routing was applied again to a different call. With the HIGH above, the automated detector and all three human tracking surfaces were simultaneously silent on one shipping call site.

MEDIUM #152: the excused call fails the marker's own admission test. ALLOW_MARKER's contract at scripts/security-audit.py:392 reads 'Every use is a claim that the call survives its sunset.' The call-site justification at background.html:89-90 says the v1 call 'is expected to fail after 2027-01-01, and the v2 one below answers in its place.' The second half is false and the same file says so fifteen lines earlier: `_pushRegistered = found || !complete` with `complete` permanently false once v1 is removed makes the predicate constant true, so the v2 answer is discarded rather than used in its place. Two accurate statements sit fifteen lines apart contradicting each other, and the inaccurate one is the one the automated check reads. FIX: remove the marker and let the call flag, or add a weaker marker class ('deliberate, degrades at sunset, tracked by <issue>') that annotates without clearing. Correct the call-site comment either way.

MEDIUM #154: partner-controlled fieldId is interpolated unescaped into an innerHTML sink. main.js:858 and 860 build '<select id="cf-' + f.fieldId + '">' and the input equivalent, and addFormField assigns the result to d.innerHTML at main.js:874. `f` comes from GET /v1/forms/company/{id}, the partner organization's own process-form definition, and the UI runs in the Zendesk agent's authenticated session. Every sibling value in the same block is escaped (f.label via esc(), option values via esc(o) at line 857); only fieldId is not. The only thing between this and XSS is FieldMetadataDTO.fieldId being typed integer in the spec, which the client never checks and which is nowhere documented as a relied-on invariant - while the same file documents exactly that reasoning for collab.token at main.js:381-383. Not exploited: whether TSANet storage permits a non-integer fieldId to reach a client was not probed. Severity rests on the undocumented reliance. FIX: parseInt and skip non-finite, so the getElementById lookup at main.js:889 still agrees.

MEDIUM #155: background.html:178 retries a 401 with no guard, unlike main.js:155 and :175. The delta edited this exact line to add the version argument and did not add the guard. getJwt() rejects when login fails, so a bad password terminates; the unbounded case is a login that succeeds followed by a business call that still returns 401, which never rejects, so pollForInboundCases's .catch never runs and setInterval starts another non-terminating chain every 60 seconds in every open tab. CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD'S PREVIOUS ENTRY: it asserted this was reachable today via a credential lacking ROLE_API. That is FALSE and was written without probing it. Probed on BETA with the sdk1 admin user (authenticates, no API role): GET /v1/me 200, GET /v1/collaboration-requests?type=INBOUND 403, GET /v1/webhooks 403, body type https://api.tsanet.org/errors/access-denied. A 403 falls through to `if (!res.ok) throw` and terminates cleanly. No reachable-today trigger has been identified. The finding stands on the missing guard, the asymmetry with main.js, and the post-sunset case where a retired route answering 401 rather than 404/410 would trigger it.

LOW #156: sanitizeHtml's allowlist consults the prototype chain. ALLOWED is an object literal and membership is `if (ALLOWED[child.tagName])` at main.js:1182, so any Object.prototype key that is a valid lowercase tag name passes. Confirmed in headless Chrome: <svg><constructor onload=...>hi</constructor></svg> sanitizes to <constructor>hi</constructor>. Not exploitable - attributes are stripped unconditionally for every tag except A, so the surviving element is inert, and 18 payloads including the standard mXSS corpus were all inert with javascript: and data: hrefs removed and target/rel forced. Reported because the allowlist is not the allowlist it appears to be, and the only thing making that harmless is one edit away. FIX: hasOwnProperty, or make ALLOWED a Set.

LOW #157: stripHtml decodes entities AFTER stripping tags, so its output can contain live markup. main.js:1209. Confirmed: stripHtml('<img src=x onerror=1>') returns the string . All six call sites are currently safe and each was checked (474/475 wrap in esc(); 504 is normForMatch, comparison only; 553/554 feed a Zendesk comment.body, which is plain text not html_body; 465 is escaped at 475). Latent, not live. FIX: rename to htmlToText and return escaped text, or drop the entity decode; the name should not promise safety the function does not provide.

LOW #158: the v1_base gate is keyed to one literal spelling of the version default. `\|\|\s*['\"]v1['\"]` matches the text `|| 'v1'`; rewriting baseUrl as `(version ? version : 'v1')` or `(version ?? 'v1')` is semantically identical, still defaults to v1, and turns on_v1_base false so both needs_v1_base patterns gate off. Verified by mutation: with that rewrite and the marker removed, background.html's live v1 call is not reported. Mitigating and also verified: if the refactor leaves the marker in place, the stale-marker WARN fires and names the file, so the check only goes fully silent if the marker is removed in the same edit. FIX: assert the invariant rather than infer it - fail if no file under zaf-build/ matches v1_base.

RESOLVED SAME DAY: the LOW that closing #144 removed the 2027-01-01 deadline from release.yml's view. #144 was reopened 2026-07-29 and the gate sees it again as security,high-priority. Note the deadlock this creates and that it is deliberate: #144 cannot close until a release exists, and the gate flags on #144 until it closes, so cutting v1.0.56 requires accepting #144 explicitly for that release.
MEDIUM #140: an uncovered release is easy to accept repeatedly. OPEN, accepted by Shawn 2026-07-28.
MEDIUM #96: durable audit trail. OPEN, accepted.
MEDIUM #119: move the ZAF app off the TSANet API user password to the ZIS Entra client credential. OPEN, accepted.
LOW #98: note attribution heuristic remains open pending Connect-API-Code#131. OPEN, accepted.
notes: Extends the record from 52dcea4 to 8aa9f7a (v1.0.56 in the manifest, NOT in any release). Unlike the previous two rounds this delta contains real executable change to the shipped bundle: #148 (4dbbf4d) and #149 (8aa9f7a).

TWO PASSES, and the second is why this record is worth reading. The first was written by the author of both code commits, who also wrote both PR descriptions, closed #144, filed #150, and graded all of it. The second was run cold from a separate session against 8aa9f7a, deliberately pointed at that commit so the record it read was the 52dcea4-era one and it could not see the first pass's conclusions. It found NINE findings to the first pass's four, independently reached the same HIGH from a cold start, and proved one of the first pass's findings wrong on evidence. Where the two disagree, the independent pass is what is recorded here.

THE FIRST PASS PUT A FALSE CLAIM IN THIS RECORD, and how it got there matters more than the claim. Its 401 finding asserted the loop was reachable today through a credential lacking ROLE_API. An advisor call had proposed that rescope, it was persuasive, and it was written into a security record WITHOUT being probed. The independent pass probed it: 403, not 401, so the path terminates cleanly. Re-probed a third time by the original author to confirm before correcting: sdk1 admin user on BETA returns /me 200, /collaboration-requests 403, /webhooks 403. This is the taxonomy's first rule failing in the artifact the taxonomy produces, and it is recorded rather than quietly edited out.

THE LARGEST MISS WAS NOT A SUBTLE ONE. No release exists. v1.0.54 is the newest tag and Release; the fix is in main and in no installable artifact, so every member is running the fail-open probe today. The first pass wrote the sentence 'no 1.0.55 was ever released' in a PR body and did not take the next step. This is a known recurring failure mode in this repo, documented as such, and knowing it did not prevent repeating it. #144 has been reopened with a release acceptance criterion.

CATEGORY CLAIMS FROM THE FIRST PASS THAT WERE WRONG: it marked categories 1 and 7 clean. Category 1 carries the release finding. Category 7 carries three: the unescaped fieldId, the prototype-chain allowlist, and stripHtml. The first pass explicitly declined to re-review the pre-existing sinks and then marked the category clean anyway, which is the exact shape of the thing it had just criticised itself for elsewhere. The independent pass inventoried all 22 innerHTML sinks, confirmed no outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/document.write/eval/new Function, and ran an 18-payload mXSS suite in headless Chrome.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED, not inherited: SRI computed by fetching zaf_sdk 2.0.37 and hashing it, matching the integrity attribute in all three HTML files; all three GitHub Actions pinned to full 40-char SHAs; release.yml permissions {} with jobs opting in; no ${{ }} in any run: body; tsanet_password the only secure parameter, consumed via server-side proxy substitution; domainWhitelist exactly the two connect2 hosts; secret scan across js/json/html/py/md clean; GET /v1/webhooks and GET /v2/webhooks both 200 on BETA today with NO Deprecation, Sunset, Link or Warning response header, so the deadline stays invisible at runtime and the RFC 8594 header remains TSANet's to add.

EVERY FALSIFIABLE CLAIM IN BOTH PR DESCRIPTIONS WAS CHECKED by the independent pass and held: the plain-array vs PagedResponse shapes, the 79/79 and 42/42 identical counts and key sets across v1 and v2, the BETA subscription probe (id 55, BASIC, active, payloadVersion V1) against an empty v2 collection, callbackAuthType present on WebhookSubscriptionV2DTO, the 14/0/1 mechanical tally at exit 2 under --no-network, all four audit-allow conditions, and the negative lookahead. The technical work in both PRs is sound; the findings are about what the delta's tracking and gating leave behind, and about pre-existing code it did not touch.

NOT VERIFIED: whether TSANet storage permits a non-integer fieldId to reach a client; the 401 recursion against a live 401-returning endpoint; what status GET /v1/webhooks returns after removal (404, 410 or 401, and a 401 would trigger the loop); release.yml's behaviour under a FAILING audit, still carried unresolved and reachable on 2026-10-03; #138's fix, verified by inspection not by pushing a hostile tag; PROD runtime, since PROD credentials are known-dead; whether GuardCreate (#41) absorbs the duplicate condition the v1.0.54 fail-open path creates today; the docx, ZIS Quick Start and GitBook surfaces this round.

SCHEDULED TIGHTENING, carried forward: from 2026-10-03, 90 days before the 2027-01-01 sunset, check_deprecated_endpoints() begins returning FAIL. The HIGH above is that this tightening can be silently defeated by a marked call, so the date should not be relied on as the backstop it was designed to be.

FILED 2026-07-29 on Shawn's go: #151 (high), #152, #153, #154, #155 (medium), #156, #157, #158 (low). The ninth finding, that no release exists, is not filed separately; it is the release acceptance criterion on the reopened #144. #153 supersedes #144's close comment routing the probe call to #101, and a correction was posted on #101 noting that the same wrong routing has now been made against that issue twice. GATE CONSEQUENCE, stated because it is the whole point of filing: #144, #151, #152, #153, #154 and #155 are open, labelled security, and not accepted, so release.yml's findings check now flags on six issues. The three LOWs are reported and do not flag. Cutting v1.0.56 requires accepting the blocking set explicitly. That is a deliberate deadlock: #144 cannot close until a release exists, and it blocks the release until it closes.
